title: Posterolateral Elbow Dislocation: MRI Study of Ligament and Muscle Healing
official: Posterolateral Elbow Dislocation: MRI Study of Ligament and Muscle Healing
summary:
The goal of this prospective observational study is to evaluate the healing of the medial collateral ligament (MCL) and associated muscle injuries following posterolateral elbow dislocation using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

The main question the study aims to answer is:

\* What proportion of patients with posterolateral elbow dislocation have a healed MCL at 12 months, based on MRI assessment?

The study will also assess MCL healing at 6 months and evaluate elbow pain, functional recovery, range of motion, stiffness, clinical instability, and ulnar nerve neuropathy at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months. The study will investigate whether patient characteristics and clinical factors are associated with ligament and muscle healing, persistent instability, stiffness, or functional outcomes.

Participants will undergo clinical and radiological assessments at inclusion, including evaluation of pain, elbow function, range of motion, elbow stability, and ulnar nerve symptoms. An initial MRI will be performed within 2 to 10 days after injury to document early tissue damage. Follow-up MRI and clinical assessments will be performed at 6 and 12 months.

The primary outcome will be the rate of MCL healing at 12 months, determined by qualitative MRI assessment by a radiologist. The MCL will be classified as either "Healed" or "Not healed".
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adult over 18 years of age.
* Patients who had a simple dislocation of the elbow dated 15 days or less (i.e., without associated fracture) that can be reduced by closed means. Presence of a dislocation and absence of fracture(s) will be confirmed by a plain X-ray.
* Patients who had an MRI scan after elbow dislocation.
* Patient who has given non-opposition to this research.
* Patient affiliated to/or beneficiary of a social security scheme.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Adult over 75 years old.
* Patient refusing to participate in the study.
* Pregnant and breastfeeding women.
* Polytraumatized patients.
* Recurrent or open dislocation.
* Additional traumatic injuries to the affected arm.
* Surgical intervention for the treatment of the initial elbow dislocation prior to study inclusion.
* Impaired elbow function prior to trauma (i.e., stiff or painful elbow or neurological disorder such as inflammatory arthritis).
* Previous operations or fractures involving the elbow.
* Patients who have been previously diagnosed with an upper limb neuromuscular disease.
* Protected patient: an adult under guardianship, curatorship or other legal protection, deprived of liberty by judicial or administrative decision.
